attribution.note: Marcus explicitly includes himself in the shared expectation.

semantics.note: An unqualified expectation of substantial coding impact is a forecast. The normalisation adds no productivity or employment commitment.

contract.note: Substantial changes in ordinary programming workflows are a fair plain reading of big impact. The contextual five-year horizon comes from the panel framing; early fulfillment requires broad actual integration.

evidence.note: The October survey documents widespread coding-tool integration. Its daily-use denominator must be read with e2: users of coding assistants or agents, not all developers.
Daily use among 73% of coding-assistant users, alongside actual code generation and debugging, establishes routine integration at substantial scale.
Selection problems limit productivity estimates. The earlier slowdown concerns a different period and does not contradict substantial workflow changes.

reviews.rationale: The October 6 survey findings meet the early-resolution rule through broad, routine use in actual coding tasks. This supports substantial workflow impact without establishing productivity gains, improved quality, or employment displacement. METR's measurement cautions do not overturn that narrower conclusion.

attribution.note: Marcus directly identifies his own position on education.

semantics.note: The statement commits to large impact. The accompanying caution is preserved and supplies neither a probabilistic hedge nor an explicit antecedent.

contract.note: Widespread changes to teaching, learning, or assessment fairly express large educational impact without requiring improvement. The five-year deadline is contextual to the panel rather than explicit in the sentence.

evidence.note: The UK undergraduate findings describe December 2025. Publication after the forecast does not make these pre-forecast assessment changes subsequent fulfillment.
The US K–12 survey supports meaningful effects through reported use and time savings. It does not establish the frequency or magnitude of changes to ordinary teaching, learning, or assessment.
Limited formal guidance constrains claims of institutional transformation but does not contradict large impact through informal educational practices.

reviews.rationale: The contextual February 2031 deadline remains ahead. Available post-statement evidence supports adoption and perceived benefits but does not establish substantial practice changes meeting the early-resolution rule. The strongest assessment-change finding predates the forecast. Limited institutional guidance does not establish failure.
